nodes.description: For severe airway involvement refractory to medical therapy, interventional procedures (airway stenting, tracheostomy, non-invasive ventilation) provide structural support. Stenting is reserved as a last resort because it carries high rates of complications (granulation tissue, mucostasis) and is associated with worse survival; early biologic therapy is preferred to avoid it.

nodes.description: Loss of tolerance to cartilage matrix produces both humoral and cellular autoimmunity. This adaptive arm orchestrates the downstream effector inflammation.

nodes.description: A distinct, parallel mechanism operates in a subset (~8%) of patients given a clinical diagnosis of relapsing polychondritis. Somatic mutations at methionine-41 of UBA1 in myeloid-lineage cells dysregulate ubiquitylation and drive a myeloid/innate-immune-predominant systemic autoinflammation (VEXAS syndrome) that produces chondritis clinically indistinguishable from classic RP. Unlike the HLA-driven adaptive pathway, this arm is hematopoietic and autoinflammatory rather than autoimmune, and feeds into the same innate effector phase.
